ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: On the left side of the figure is capacitor C1, and on the right side is capacitor C2; the lower terminals of the two capacitors are connected by the same wire. The upper terminals of the two capacitors are respectively connected to the top wire, but there is a switch S in the middle, and the switch in the figure was originally open. After S is closed, the upper terminals of the two capacitors are also connected together, so C1 and C2 become connected in parallel, and there is no external power supply. Reasoning: According to the problem statement, initially the voltage across C1 is 55 V, and C2 is regarded as initially uncharged. After the switch is closed, the system is isolated, and total charge is conserved. The initial charge is Q_initial = C1 × 55. Finally the two parallel capacitors have the same voltage V_final, so Q_final = (C1 + C2) × V_final. Set the two equal: C1 × 55 = (C1 + C2) × V_final. Substituting C1 = 100 μF and C2 = 10 μF gives V_final = 100 × 55 / (100 + 10) = 5500 / 110 = 50 V. Therefore after the switch is closed, the voltage drop across C1 is 50 V.
